name: Red Flags When Hiring an ADU Design Contractor in LA County

mainEntity.name: What red flags indicate an ADU design contractor in Los Angeles County may be underestimating costs or overselling approvals?
mainEntity.text: What red flags indicate an ADU design contractor in Los Angeles County may be underestimating costs or overselling approvals?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because ADU demand is high across Los Angeles County, some designers oversell their services or underestimate complexity to win work. Watch for several common red flags. Extremely low design fees paired with a vague or one-page scope often mean critical elements like structural engineering, Title 24, or permit coordination are excluded and will be billed later as extras. Be wary of anyone promising “guaranteed approval” or a specific maximum unit size before they have reviewed your zoning, lot size, overlays, and utility conditions; approval depends on factors they cannot fully control. If a contractor refuses to discuss realistic construction cost ranges based on recent jobs, or quotes figures far below what most local builders charge, you may be looking at a bait-and-switch situation. Ask for addresses or permit numbers of ADUs they have actually designed and permitted in your city or unincorporated area; vague or unverified claims are a concern. Overly optimistic timelines, such as “we do everything in 30 days” for complex lots, are another sign they may not understand jurisdictional realities. Finally, if there is no written limit on plan revisions or plan-check responses, you could face open-ended hourly bills later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Red flags include very low design fees with vague scope, promises of “guaranteed approval” without reviewing your property records, refusal to discuss likely construction cost ranges, and lack of recent, verifiable ADU permits in your jurisdiction. Overly optimistic timelines and no written revision limits are also warning signs.
